cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code constructs a path using untrusted header.linkname from tar archive and resolves it without validation, then reads the file content when hardlink creation fails

connection.evidence: header.linkname (external input from tar archive) -> path.resolve(cwd, header.linkname) -> srcpath -> xfs.createReadStream(srcpath) -> file content read

diff_causality.evidence: This line is the fallback mechanism that reads arbitrary files when hardlink creation fails. Without this line, the fallback to file reading would not occur

security_control.evidence: Path validation is missing for header.linkname before resolving and reading files
security_control.required_control: Path validation and sanitization to restrict file access to intended directories
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-22 requires validating that resolved paths remain within intended boundaries to prevent directory traversal
existing_controls_checked: path.resolve() normalizes but doesn't restrict traversal
No observed validation of header.linkname against traversal patterns
security_control.deficiency_evidence: header.linkname is used directly in path.resolve without checking for '../' sequences or restricting to safe directories

concrete_impact.evidence: Arbitrary file read from the filesystem when processing malicious tar archives with crafted linknames

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the hardlink fallback mechanism would not read arbitrary files when link creation fails with EPERM, eliminating the path traversal vulnerability in the fallback scenario
supporting_evidence: header.linkname comes from untrusted tar archive input
path.resolve(cwd, header.linkname) creates srcpath without validation
xfs.createReadStream(srcpath) reads arbitrary files based on uncontrolled input
Fallback mechanism activates on EPERM error with hardlinkAsFilesFallback option
unresolved_facts: Whether upstream tar-stream validation exists for linkname paths
Default value and typical usage of hardlinkAsFilesFallback option
Any additional filesystem-level access controls that might restrict reads
review_comment: The hardlink fallback mechanism reads arbitrary files using untrusted header.linkname from tar archives without path validation. When hardlink creation fails with EPERM, the code resolves header.linkname against cwd and reads the resulting file, enabling directory traversal attacks. Validate header.linkname to ensure it doesn't contain path traversal sequences before using it in path resolution.
